question: Do public records expose the historical Bulaklakin Reef fish assessments or usable sanctuary boundary geometry?

sourceReviews.title: State of the Coasts of Cavite Province
sourceReviews.provider: PEMSEA; Provincial Government Environment and Natural Resources Office, Cavite

findings.surveyInventory: Table 5 lists a 2005 Refined Risk Assessment of Bulaklakin Reef Fish Sanctuary led by DA-BFAR and the Ternate LGU. The table records that the assessment occurred, not its fish observations or methods.
findings.governanceContext: Table 18 records Ternate Ordinance No. 04 S-2005 and Resolution No. 17 S-2005 concerning municipal fish-sanctuary and marine-reserve areas, including Bulaklakin Reef. This is historical document context and does not verify current legal status or boundaries.
findings.limits: The report does not provide the underlying 2005 assessment, fish taxa, survey stations, coordinates, vouchers, or item-specific data-reuse terms.

sourceReviews.title: Conservation and Protection of Bulaklakin Reef Fish Sanctuary
sourceReviews.provider: UNDP Global Environment Facility Small Grants Programme

findings.access: Official project page text was available in the public search index, but a direct open returned HTTP 403; no local page snapshot or underlying report was retrieved.
findings.historicalAssessmentLead: The indexed project description says an April 2005 rapid risk assessment reported live corals and fishes over 37-40% of the reef area. The wording does not yield fish taxa, counts, method, or an independently auditable denominator.
findings.laterSurveyLead: The indexed page says Anak ng Dagat facilitated a survey of the reef through BFAR in 2008 and reports only qualitative improvement relative to the 2005 survey. The underlying 2008 survey and any species table were not located.
findings.plannedOutputs: The project page lists a five-year management plan and sanctuary boundary markings among expected outputs; this does not demonstrate that a verified boundary file or final management plan is publicly available.

sourceReviews.title: Geographical Coordinates of Bulaklakin Reef Fish Sanctuary in Ternate Cavite
sourceReviews.provider: Freedom of Information Philippines; Biodiversity Management Bureau (DENR-BMB)

findings.request: A public request dated 2022-04-14 asks BMB for exact Bulaklakin sanctuary boundaries or coordinates; the portal marks it successful on 2022-05-10.
findings.responseVisibility: The visible transcript contains a generic statement that a copy is enclosed, followed by the requester asking where the attachment is. The page rendering reviewed here exposes no coordinate values or downloadable boundary attachment.
findings.decision: A successful status on this public request is not itself a coordinate dataset. No geometry was reconstructed or adopted from the transcript.

findings.reefStatusContext: The profile's Table 2.8 labels coral reefs in Ternate municipal waters as 'For Assessment' in its 2022 status table. This does not identify Bulaklakin as the same assessment site or provide a fish survey result.
findings.nameBoundary: The profile's provincial reef locator and 2022 status summary do not provide a Bulaklakin sanctuary polygon or crosswalk the 2020 Senemento/Sementeno RRA lead to Bulaklakin.

queries: Conservation and Protection of Bulaklakin Reef Fish Sanctuary fish species survey
Bulaklakin Reef Ternate fish survey 2008 BFAR
Bulaklakin Rapid Resource Assessment fish Cavite report
Senemento Reef Ternate fish survey fish sanctuary BFAR
boundedSearch.outcome: The search located an official Cavite coastal-assessment inventory and indexed project-page summaries naming the 2005 risk assessment and 2008 BFAR survey, but did not retrieve either underlying assessment or its taxon/station data. A 2022 BMB FOI boundary request is labeled successful, yet the public transcript has no visible attachment or coordinates. Search failure does not prove that assessment files or boundary data are unavailable elsewhere.
limits: The UNDP GEF SGP page could not be opened directly; only its indexed official page text was reviewed.
The FOI transcript is evidence of a retrieval attempt and missing publicly visible attachment, not the boundary itself.
Historical reef assessments do not establish present fish presence, habitat condition, current rules, catchability, or safety.
No candidate name has been crosswalked to Senemento/Sementeno Reef or Maragondon-area reef/river features.

rightsReview.decision: Keep minimal attributed bibliography and retrieval facts only. Do not copy assessment tables, maps, coordinates, or project-page imagery into the app without source access and item-specific review.

nextAction: Continue independent CALABARZON fish-evidence work while awaiting any separately authorized BFAR response. If Joseph chooses to send the prepared draft, ask for the 2005/2008 Bulaklakin assessment tables or final reports, taxon/station/date/method crosswalk, boundary attachment in its native CRS, underlying ordinances/technical descriptions, and item-specific reuse terms. Do not treat the old public FOI status as boundary data or merge Bulaklakin with Senemento/Sementeno without an authoritative crosswalk.
